Count regression model specification for tidymodels

Source: R/parsnip-count_reg.R
count_reg.Rd

count_reg() defines a count regression model for the parsnip package. Every estimator of flexCountReg is an engine, so all of them can be used in workflows, resampling, tuning and workflow sets. The count distribution (family) is a main argument.

Usage

count_reg(mode = "regression", family = NULL, engine = "flexCountReg")

# S3 method for class 'count_reg'
update(object, parameters = NULL, family = NULL, fresh = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

mode

the model mode; only "regression" is available.

family

the count distribution, one of the family values of countreg (for example "NB2", "PIG2" or "PLN") or a family from new_count_family(). NULL uses the default of the engine's estimator ("NB2" for countreg()). The engines "renb", "repois" and "poislind_re" have a fixed distribution and do not accept it; "negmultinom" and "countreg_fe" accept the families of their estimators; "countreg_mv" accepts one family per outcome.

engine

the fitting engine; see the section Engines.

object

a count_reg() specification.

parameters

a one-row tibble or named list of main arguments to update.

fresh

logical; replace the arguments (TRUE) or modify them?

...

engine arguments to update.

Value

A count_reg model specification.

Engines

EngineEstimatorModel
"flexCountReg"countregany family, with zero-inflated, hurdle and underreporting components
"countreg_rp"countreg_rprandom parameters
"countreg_mix"countreg_mixfinite mixtures
"countreg_lc"countreg_lclatent classes
"countreg_fe"countreg_fefixed effects
"countreg_hier"countreg_hierhierarchical models
"countreg_alloc"countreg_alloctotal plus allocation (several outcome columns)
"countreg_mv"countreg_mvmultivariate (several outcomes)
"renb"renbrandom-effects negative binomial
"repois"repoisrandom-effects Poisson
"poislind_re"poislind_rerandom-effects Poisson-Lindley
"negmultinom"negmultinomnegative multinomial

All other arguments of the estimator are engine arguments, set with parsnip::set_engine(), for example set_engine("countreg_rp", rpar_formula = ~ -1 + x, ndraws = 200). Arguments with a finite set of choices have tuning parameters (see count_family).

The estimators' own engine argument (the numerical method) is called fit_engine here, for example set_engine("countreg_hier", fit_engine = "laplace").

The engine argument predict_args (a list) holds arguments passed to the model's predict() method for numeric predictions and intervals, for example predict_args = list(method = "Exact") for "countreg_rp", list(newgroup = "mean_fe") for "countreg_fe" or list(marginal = TRUE) for "countreg_hier".

Formulas, recipes and extra columns

The engines use the formula interface. In a workflow, the model receives only the columns the preprocessor declares as outcomes and predictors (not those with other roles), so every column the model needs must be a predictor: offsets, grouping variables, and variables of auxiliary formulas (dis_param_formula_1, rpar_formula, ...). Two ways to say which of them enter the mean model:

  • Give the model formula, as in workflows::add_model(spec, formula = y ~ x + offset(log_exp)), with workflows::add_variables() or a recipe as the preprocessor. This works for every model, including smooths (s(x)), formula offsets, random effects ((1 | site)), tv() terms and several outcomes (cbind(y1, y2) ~ x).

  • Without a model formula, all predictors enter the mean model (y ~ .), except that columns named in offset, group_var, panel_id, cluster, fixef, cre_group or time, and the variables of rpar_formula for "countreg_rp" (which are random instead of fixed), are left out of the .. The outcome is then named ..y in the fitted model.

With a recipe, do not transform the grouping columns (for example with step_dummy() or step_normalize()) or an offset.

Case weights

Case weights are passed to the estimator's weights. By default they are frequency weights. parsnip passes the engine only their values, so for importance weights with "flexCountReg" or "countreg_rp" set the engine argument weight_type = "sampling"; a warning is given for weights that are not whole numbers without it.

Predictions

type = "numeric" gives the expected counts of the estimator's predict() method, with one row per row of new_data and NA for rows with missing values. For models with several outcomes there is one column per outcome or category (.pred_<name>); predict_args = list(type = "total") gives the total of "countreg_alloc" as .pred. The "flexCountReg" engine also has type = "conf_int" and type = "pred_int" (see predict.flexCountReg). Everything else is available with type = "raw", whose opts are passed to predict(): for example predict(fit, new_data, type = "raw", opts = list(type = "prob", max_count = 5)) for count probabilities.

Predictions that use the observed outcome (Empirical Bayes predictions of random-parameter models, posterior class probabilities) need it in new_data; a workflow removes the outcome, so use the model itself: predict(hardhat::extract_fit_engine(wf), newdata = ...). All other functions of the package (margEffTable, cureplot, rootogram, vcov(), ...) also take the extracted model.

Several outcomes

The engines "countreg_alloc" and "countreg_mv" can be fitted and predicted in workflows, but the resampling functions of tune compute metrics for one outcome, so use rsample splits directly to validate them.

Loading

Requires the parsnip package. The engines are registered when flexCountReg is loaded; load it before using a saved model or workflow. Parallel workers of tune load it themselves.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("parsnip", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spec <- count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
    parsnip::set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS")
  fit <- parsnip::fit(spec, Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                      data = washington_roads)
  predict(fit, new_data = washington_roads[1:5, ])
  predict(fit, new_data = washington_roads[1:5, ], type = "pred_int")

  # Another estimator
  re <- count_reg() |>
    parsnip::set_engine("repois", group_var = "ID", method = "BFGS")
  fit_re <- parsnip::fit(re, Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                         data = washington_roads)
  tidy(fit_re)
}
